passages.note: Aye on Assembly concurrence in Senate amendments, the final Assembly vote on the chaptered text; 16 of 77 voting No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Operative Section 220.5 forbids local rules requiring disclosure without the pupil's consent; it does not require staff to withhold (Section 220.3 only says staff shall not be required to disclose), so rung 1 is excluded.

rows.reasoning: Quirk-Silva voted Aye on final Assembly passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), whose operative Section 220.5 bars schools and boards from enacting or enforcing any policy that would require staff to disclose a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill does not require staff to keep the information from parents, which rules out "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents unless the student consents."
